To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the guinea pig ureter is a pure CICR‐type store and the rat is a pure receptor type store.

there is a marked difference in the mechanism of Ca(2+)-release from the internal store in the guinea-pig and rat ureter: the guinea-pigs store is purely a CICR-type store and the rat store is receptor-operated.
the guinea‐pigs and rats have a different mechanism of Ca(2+) release from the internal store, the guinea‐ pigs have a CICR‐type Ca(2+) store and rats have a receptor‐coupling Ca(2+) channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the internal Ca2 + store in smooth muscle.
the mechanisms involved in the regulation of intracellular calcium concentration ([Ca2+]I) in the ureter.
the mechanisms of Ca(2+) release and uptake in the internal store of smooth muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in guinea‐pigs, the internal Ca2+-store is a CICR-type store and in rats it is a receptor-operated Ca2+-release channel.
the rat ureteral smooth muscle is a pure CICR type and the guinea‐pigs is a mixed receptor‐CICR type.

the rat ureteral smooth muscle possesses a ryanodin‐insensitive, caffeine‐ and cyclopiazonic acid‐sensitive receptor‐operated store, whereas the guinea‐ pig ureteral smooth muscles possess a ryanodinesensitive, caffeine‐and cyclopiazonic‐acid‐sensitive Ca2+‐induced Ca2+ release‐type store.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat ureter has a ryanodinesterase‐like activity which may be involved in the degradation of the ryanodine receptor, thus explaining the lack of caffeine response.
the guinea pig store is a ryanodinereceptor Ca2+ store, whereas the rat store is an IP3 receptor‐operated store.
the ureter of guinea‐pigs has a pure CICR‐type store, whereas that of rats has a mixed type of store.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rat ureter is a good model for the study of receptor‐operated stores in smooth muscle.
the rat and guinea pig ureter are very different in their ability to respond to carbachol and caffeine.
there are species differences in smooth muscle physiology and that the rat is an inappropriate animal model to use for studying smooth muscle physiology in the guinea pig.
